for background abandoned shopping carts
are a nuisance create potential hazards
to health safety and welfare of the
public
and interfere with pedestrian and
vehicular traffic
on january 26 2009 ordinance number 1172
added bmc chapter 8.18 to regulate
shopping carts and required shopping
cart providers to install containment
systems
however the unauthorized use
accumulation and storage of abandoned
shopping carts in both private and
public property has persisted throughout
the city
the california legislature enacted
provisions regulating shopping carts
that limit the city's ability to impound
shopping carts in private and public
property
however the business and professions
code authorizes local governments to
adopt regulations that are not in
conflict with the state's preempting
provisions
the proposed ordinance ensures that
owners and operators of retail
establishments providing more than five
shopping carts take reasonable measures
preventing the removal of shopping carts
from the premises
and provides for the prompt retrieval of
any removed or abandoned carts
the ordinance provisions include
requirements for signage at the business
premises and on carts
the submittal of a mandatory plan for
physical card containment
and the inclusion of a retrieval plan to
retrieve lost stolen or abandoned carts
regarding signage the signs on each
shopping cart must identify the card
owner
indicate that the unauthorized removal
or possession of the card is a violation
of the law
list the procedures for the authorized
removal from the premises
provide the contact information for the
return of the card to the rightful owner
and provide this information in both
english and spanish
regarding the mandatory plan retail
establishments with more than five cards
must prepare and submit a written plan
to prevent customers from removing
shopping carts from the owner's premises
and to retrieve shopping carts that are
removed from the premises
owners must submit the plan to the city
by march 31st 2022 along with a
processing fee that will be determined
through a separate city council
resolution
the plan must include the following
elements
physical measures such as the
installation of disabling devices on the
cards
the use of security guards to prevent
customers from removing cards from the
premises
the installation of ballers or chains
or requiring security deposits for the
use of the cards
daily card confinement requires the
establishment to collect and secure all
cards at the end of each business day
and the retrieval plan requires the
establishment to retain shopping cart
retrieval services to ensure that
streets within a two mile radius of that
establishment are patrolled for any
cards that may have been removed from
the premises
retail establishments with approved
plans are exempt from the payment of
fees that may be due for the retrieval
of cars that are impounded by the city
in regard to the impalement of carts the
city may retrieve an impound abandoned
shopping carts after a three-day notice
to the owner
or immediately by providing a 24-hour
notice of impalement
whether to retrieve or reclaim impounded
cards within three business days of
notification may result in an
administrative fine of fifty dollars for
each occurrence in excess of three
during the six month periods ending on
june 30th and on december 31st
and the currency includes the retrieval
of any cards in a one-day period
owners are required to pay the actual
cost of retrieval and impoundment if
parts are reclaimed after three business
days
parts that are not reclaimed within 30
days may be sold or disposed
the city may also contract for retrieval
services
